title: Check yourself: Adaptive thinking, extended thinking and effort

questions.stem: A team wants to cut the cost of a workload on Claude Opus 5.5 that currently thinks a lot. A developer proposes setting `thinking` to `disabled`. What does the page say?

options.text: The request returns a 400, so remove the output cap instead
options.says: Ruled out because "`max_tokens` is a strict limit" on spend and does not change how much the model thinks.

options.text: The request succeeds, and thinking stops for that call alone
options.says: Ruled out because "Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 always think adaptively and cannot be told otherwise".

options.text: The request succeeds, and thinking falls to its lowest setting
options.says: Ruled out because the lowest setting named is Sonnet 5.5's, "up-front thinking off at high effort or below", and Opus 5.5 has no such setting.

options.text: The request returns a 400, so lower the effort level instead
options.says: The model table shows "400 error" for `disabled` on Opus 5.5, and the page says to "lower effort first" to cut cost.

questions.stem: A response has a short visible reply and an `output_tokens` of 1,900. The `thinking_tokens` field reads 1,650. What is billed as output?

options.text: All 1,900 tokens, since thinking is charged even when it is not shown
options.says: The page says "You are billed for the full thinking process, not the thinking content visible in the response."

options.text: Only 250 tokens, since the thinking was hidden by the default display
options.says: Ruled out because the thinking tokens are "billed as output tokens", whether the display shows them or not.

options.text: Only 1,650 tokens, since the answer is covered by the input price
options.says: Ruled out because the page bills "the full thinking process, not the thinking content visible in the response", so the answer is not the only part charged.

options.text: About 80 tokens, since billing follows the words that are returned
options.says: Ruled out because the page says the visible text understates the bill: "So the visible text understates the bill."

questions.stem: A request on Claude Haiku 4.5 puts `low` under `output_config` to save money. What does the page back?

options.text: Haiku 4.5 takes the setting only together with a manual budget
options.says: Ruled out because the manual budget belongs to the thinking setting, and the page puts effort "in output_config, not inside thinking".

options.text: Haiku 4.5 treats `low` as its default, so the setting changes nothing
options.says: Ruled out because the default row names only Opus 5.5 and the models that support effort: "The default is high on every model that supports effort except Opus 5.5".

options.text: That model has no such control, so the setting buys no saving
options.says: The page says "Haiku 4.5 does not support effort", and the table of effort support lists the other three models.

options.text: Haiku 4.5 applies the setting to tool calls and ignores thinking
options.says: Ruled out because the page says effort "works with or without thinking" on models that support it.

origin.section: Effort: the control that replaced the budget
